content.rationale: Bottleneck Gaussian distance is sensitive to near-OOS intent shifts, while encoder-output distance captures broader domain shifts. Robust train-fitted scaling puts the two density signals on comparable additive scales without using evaluation statistics.

Training features concentrate near a principal in-scope subspace, so a large orthogonal residual identifies representations that are poorly explained by in-scope variation. Combining this ViM-style residual with energy captures both feature-space novelty and classifier uncertainty.

Agreement between normalized encoder-space and bottleneck-space neighborhood distances reduces sensitivity to a single representation while detecting queries unsupported by local in-scope examples. Using a moderately large neighborhood emphasizes intent-region support rather than exact duplicate matching.

OOS queries can deviate along low-variance within-class directions that are suppressed by standard principal-subspace methods. A train-calibrated trailing-eigenspace score emphasizes these locally constrained directions.

OOS queries often lack a clearly dominant class-conditional feature match, producing a small gap between their nearest and second-nearest Gaussian class distances. This boundary-ambiguity score differs from minimum-distance density by emphasizing competition among classes rather than absolute proximity.

OOS inputs often have a smaller separation between the two most competitive intent logits than in-scope examples. Class-conditional robust calibration accounts for intents with naturally ambiguous decision boundaries.

L2-normalized class prototypes measure angular support for each query, making OOS items with weak semantic alignment to every intent score highly. Averaging each class prototype from training data makes the score robust to individual examples.

Energy and encoder-space Mahalanobis distance capture complementary classifier uncertainty and representation novelty. Train-fitted quantile-sigmoid calibration places both signals on a common bounded scale without using evaluation statistics.

In-scope examples tend to exhibit class-specific Dirichlet concentration profiles, including evidence strength, predictive concentration entropy, and top-class dominance. OOS inputs can have atypical profiles even when their total evidence alone (vacuity) appears in-distribution.

Energy remains the dominant signal for confidently in-scope queries, while a train-calibrated encoder Mahalanobis distance is increasingly emphasized as energy indicates classifier uncertainty. This conditional fusion avoids applying representation novelty equally to already confident predictions.

Class-specific diagonal variances retain intent-dependent feature scales that a tied covariance discards, while shrinkage toward global variance stabilizes small classes. OOS queries should have high minimum shrunk diagonal Gaussian surprise across all known intents.

Class-mean differences define directions used to separate known intents in the bottleneck representation. OOS queries with unusually large energy outside this discriminative subspace are poorly explained by the intent classifier's learned structure.

Class-conditional density percentiles measure whether a query is unusually far from the intent predicted by the classifier, rather than only from its nearest Gaussian class. Bottleneck and encoder-space percentiles are additively fused with train-fitted stability weights, retaining sensitivity to both near-intent and broad-domain OOS shifts.
After removing the predicted intent's training mean, in-scope queries should lie near shared within-intent principal variation, while OOS queries retain a larger orthogonal residual.

A query may receive a confident intent prediction while lacking local support among examples of that predicted intent. Class-conditional cosine neighbourhood distance measures this predicted-intent support rather than allowing nearby examples from competing intents to mask novelty.

Low-variance within-class directions encode tightly constrained in-scope structure, so OOS queries should have unusually large trailing-subspace residuals. Combining independently calibrated bottleneck and encoder residual percentiles reduces reliance on a single representation.

A query can be confidently assigned to an intent while lying unusually far from that predicted intent's angular prototype. Class-conditional robust calibration accounts for intents with different within-class semantic spread.

The centered logit-vector norm measures overall class-separation strength while being invariant to additive logit shifts. Class-conditional robust calibration flags queries whose logit concentration is atypically weak or unusually extreme for their predicted intent.

Softmax-weighted cosine support measures alignment with the intent prototypes favored by the classifier rather than only the single nearest prototype. OOS queries should have weak aggregate angular support among plausible in-scope intents.

Low maximum-softmax confidence and weak angular alignment with the classifier-predicted intent capture complementary uncertainty and semantic-support failures. Train-fitted empirical percentiles place both signals on a shared scale without using evaluation statistics.

The normalized shape of the Dirichlet concentration vector describes how evidence is distributed among intents independently of total evidence. OOS queries can have an atypical class-specific evidence composition even when their vacuity or energy appears in-distribution.

Energy is retained for confident predictions, while a predicted-intent bottleneck Mahalanobis distance increasingly determines the score when energy indicates uncertainty. This can expose uncertain queries that are not locally compatible with their assigned intent.

Intent-specific diagonal variances preserve feature dimensions that are tightly constrained for one intent but variable for another. Shrinking each class variance toward the global variance stabilizes sparse intents while making OOS queries have high minimum class-conditional Gaussian surprise.

Known intents should concentrate much of their representation variation in the between-intent discriminative subspace, while OOS queries retain unusually large residual energy orthogonal to that subspace. Predicted-intent conditional calibration accounts for different residual spreads across intents.

Bottleneck density is sensitive to near-OOS examples that violate learned intent structure, while encoder density captures broader domain shifts. Train-fitted robust scale weights make their additive surprises comparable without using evaluation-set statistics.

ViM-style residual norm measures representation energy outside the dominant in-scope encoder subspace, where unfamiliar queries should retain more variation. A train-calibrated energy term preserves classifier uncertainty when residual novelty is weak.

OOS queries should be both distant from the in-scope cosine neighbourhood and poorly supported by neighbours sharing the classifier's predicted intent. Local predicted-intent agreement adds neighbourhood-label structure that a distance-only kNN score misses.
Low-variance within-class bottleneck directions encode constrained intent-specific structure, so OOS queries should have unusually large residual energy in this trailing subspace.

In-scope examples should have their classifier-predicted intent agree with the nearest class Gaussian prototype. OOS queries can be geometrically closer to another intent than the confidently predicted one, yielding an unusually large predicted-versus-alternative distance gap.

Temperature-softened logit entropy measures ambiguity across several plausible intents rather than only the winning class. OOS queries should retain broader tempered class uncertainty, and predicted-intent calibration accounts for classes with intrinsically different logit shapes.

In-scope features should not only align with a known class prototype but should usually have a clear angular preference over competing prototypes. OOS queries can have both weak nearest-prototype alignment and a small nearest-versus-runner-up cosine margin.

Energy captures classifier uncertainty while bottleneck Mahalanobis distance measures departure from learned intent geometry. Train-fitted empirical CDFs put both signals on a common robust scale before combining them.

The centered log-ratio of Dirichlet concentrations captures how evidential mass is distributed among intents while removing total-evidence magnitude. OOS inputs can have an atypical predicted-intent evidence composition even when vacuity or energy is normal.

Energy is most informative for confidently classified queries, while feature-space departure becomes more reliable as classifier uncertainty rises. A train-fitted energy percentile softly routes uncertain items toward full encoder Mahalanobis surprise without using evaluation-set statistics.

A query assigned to an intent should also be plausible under that intent's own diagonal feature distribution, including dimensions whose variance is unusually tight for that class. Shrinkage and predicted-class robust calibration stabilize class-specific surprise for sparse intents.

Removing the class-mean discriminative subspace leaves within-intent residual structure that should be locally supported by training queries, whereas OOS queries often have unusual residual variation.
After removing the classifier-predicted intent prototype, in-scope queries should lie near the principal within-intent variation subspace, while OOS queries retain larger residual norm.

A multi-scale cosine neighbourhood score combines the radius needed to reach many in-scope examples with local neighbourhood expansion. OOS queries should be both farther from in-scope support and less locally concentrated than typical training queries.

Low-variance within-intent directions encode tightly constrained intent structure. A query should have close same-predicted-intent neighbours in this trailing subspace, while OOS queries tend to lack such local support.
An in-scope query should be geometrically typical of the class selected by the classifier, whereas OOS queries can be confidently assigned to a class while remaining far from that class's prototype.

OOS queries often have a smaller gap between their two most plausible intents, even when total logit energy remains high. Predicted-intent conditional calibration accounts for classes with inherently broader or narrower in-scope decision margins.

Maximum softmax uncertainty and bottleneck-space Gaussian distance capture complementary classifier and representation novelty. Train empirical CDF calibration puts both signals on a shared robust percentile scale without inspecting evaluation-set statistics.

The normalized Dirichlet concentration vector describes how evidential mass is distributed across intents independently of total evidence. OOS queries should often have unusually diffuse evidence composition relative to in-scope examples predicted as the same intent.

Low-energy queries retain the classifier's confident energy ranking, while high-energy uncertain queries are increasingly judged by departure along tightly constrained trailing bottleneck directions. This routes ambiguous examples toward representation novelty without using evaluation-set calibration.

A classifier-selected intent should also have competitive likelihood under a class-specific diagonal covariance model with shrinkage for sparse classes. OOS queries can be confidently assigned to one intent while fitting another intent's feature geometry better.
The span of class means contains directions most useful for separating known intents, so in-scope examples should have class-typical residual energy after that span is removed.

A global principal subspace captures common in-scope encoder variation, while the residual norm measures feature content unsupported by that subspace. Combining train-calibrated residual novelty with energy retains classifier uncertainty information for samples that remain close to the broad in-scope manifold.

A query should be locally supported by training examples from the intent predicted by the classifier, not merely by examples from any intent. Class-conditional cosine kNN distance exposes confidently predicted queries that lie outside the local support of their assigned in-scope intent.

Trailing within-class covariance directions encode variations that are tightly constrained across known intents. A robust log-penalty for predicted-class residuals in those directions emphasizes atypical constraint violations without reducing to the usual quadratic trailing-energy ranking.

A query can be confidently assigned to an intent while its representation is closer to a different intent prototype. Predicted-class Mahalanobis surprise plus geometric disagreement exposes such mismatches.

After removing the logit offset and scale, in-scope queries assigned to an intent should retain a class-typical relative logit shape. OOS queries can have plausible confidence yet an unusual pattern of competing intent logits, producing larger angular deviation from the predicted-class prototype.

In-scope representations should align closely with the normalized prototype of their classifier-predicted intent. OOS queries can be assigned confidently while having weak cosine agreement with that intent's typical feature direction.
Logit energy and pooled-space Mahalanobis novelty capture complementary OOS signals. Train-only empirical percentile calibration makes their upper-tail evidence comparable before fusion.

The centered log-ratio shape of Dirichlet concentrations captures relative evidential allocation across intents independently of total evidence. OOS queries may have an atypical pattern of competing class evidence even when their vacuity or energy appears in-distribution.
Classifier energy is retained for confident queries, while queries in the uncertain energy tail are increasingly scored by pooled-space distance from known intent geometry.

OOS queries can violate a small number of tightly constrained, intent-specific representation coordinates even when their overall distance is moderate. A shrunk per-class diagonal variance model highlights these unusually large studentized residuals without collapsing them into a standard Gaussian density.
Removing the class-mean discriminative subspace leaves within-intent residual variation, where in-scope queries should retain local training support and OOS queries should be isolated.

A ViM-style residual norm measures feature energy outside the dominant in-scope principal subspace. Conditioning its robust calibration on the classifier-predicted intent accounts for classes with different residual variability.
Multi-scale cosine kNN distances in a train-fitted low-rank pooled representation measure whether a query has local support across both dense and broader in-scope neighborhoods.

Within-class trailing covariance directions are tightly constrained for known intents. A class-conditioned upper-tail calibration of trailing-direction residual energy highlights violations that are atypical for the classifier-selected intent.
In-scope representations tend to be substantially closer to one class prototype than to the runner-up prototype, while OOS representations often have similarly weak support from multiple intents.

OOS queries often have a smaller separation between their leading and runner-up intent logits than training examples assigned to the same predicted intent. Class-conditional train-fitted margin calibration preserves intent-specific confidence geometry beyond energy or maximum probability.

Cosine agreement with a class prototype should be high for in-scope items, but raw agreement is not comparable across intents with different directional spread. A train-fitted class-conditional robust calibration makes low prototype alignment unusually suspicious relative to the classifier-selected intent.

The normalized Dirichlet concentration vector has an evidential allocation shape independent of total evidence. OOS queries may exhibit atypical dominance, runner-up support, or entropy relative to the predicted intent even when vacuity is unremarkable.

For logits that are typical for their predicted intent, the score preserves energy ordering. When class-conditional energy becomes uncertain, it smoothly switches toward pooled-space Mahalanobis novelty.

A classifier-selected intent should fit a query better than its strongest logit rival under that intent's own shrunk diagonal covariance. OOS queries can retain a confident prediction while the runner-up intent provides equal or better heteroscedastic feature support.

Class-mean directions contain the representation components most useful for separating known intents. After removing that discriminative subspace, OOS queries should retain unusually large residual energy relative to train-fitted, predicted-intent-specific residual structure.

A ViM-style residual norm measures representation energy outside the dominant in-scope pooled-feature subspace, where OOS queries should be less well explained. Train-calibrated energy adds complementary classifier uncertainty without using evaluation-set statistics.
Averaging several raw bottleneck-space kNN radii measures both immediate local support and broader within-intent neighborhood support without relying on evaluation-set calibration.
After removing each intent prototype, low-variance within-intent directions encode tightly constrained residual structure. OOS queries should have weak local support in this trailing-eigenspace.

A query confidently assigned to an intent can still be OOS if it lies unusually far from that predicted intent's representation prototype. Class-conditional robust radius normalization avoids treating naturally diffuse intents as equally suspicious as compact ones.

The joint shape of a classifier's top-two margin and centered logit norm is intent-specific on training data. OOS inputs can have an atypical confidence magnitude or margin for their predicted intent, including overconfident extrapolations that energy or MSP may not flag.

An in-scope query should have a favorable cosine margin between the prototype of its classifier-predicted intent and competing intent prototypes. Calibrating this margin within predicted intents makes unusually weak directional commitment more suspicious without reducing to maximum prototype similarity.

Energy and pooled-space Mahalanobis distance capture complementary logit uncertainty and representation novelty. Train-fitted empirical percentile maps place both signals on a common scale before combining them.
